findings.text: The precedence this arm documents — a provenance failure outranks a NOT-JUDGED coverage and therefore exits 1, with both findings printed — is not exercised by any test: the new CLI test (`an_audit_under_a_misdeclared_rules_version_reports_coverage_not_judged`) uses the committed manifest, whose claims all carry provenance, so it only covers the "no failures" branch. A unit test passing a coverage with `not_judged: Some(..)` and a provenance-less applying row would pin `(failed.len(), open.len()) == (1, 1)` and the exit-1-beats-3 routing in `run`.
findings.title: test

findings.text: This arm restates the rules-version mismatch that the `coverage:` block and the Findings reason already print, contradicting the comment below that says the reason must have one home. Reduce this arm to the baseline summary so the NOT-JUDGED explanation is stated once (with the versions named in Findings), and drop the now-unused `crate::canon::RULES_V` interpolation.
findings.title: Report mismatch once, not three times

findings.text: This test never asserts the per-claim status or the audit verdict, so two load-bearing branches of the new audit behaviour can be deleted while the test stays green: (1) the per-claim `NOT-JUDGED` arm in `packet` — if it is removed the status falls through to `Some(_) => "uncovered"`, and `"[uncovered]"` does not contain the substring `"[covered]"`, so this assertion still passes while claims are reported as uncovered; (2) the new `verdict:` arm in `audit::run` — without it the generic "nothing here is ratified, or something ratified is uncovered" text is printed, and `stdout.contains("NOT JUDGED")` still matches the packet line. Assert both explicitly so each branch is exercised (mutation-checked).
findings.title: test

findings.text: The test only asserts the absence of `[covered]`; a regression that prints the `uncovered` arm instead of `NOT-JUDGED` for each applying claim would still pass. Assert the positive per-claim status as well so the new status arm is actually exercised.
findings.title: Assert per-claim NOT-JUDGED status explicitly

findings.text: `Coverage.not_judged` stores a pre-rendered `String`, which throws away the structured `RulesMismatch` (`manifest_rules_v`/`build_rules_v`) that `baseline.rs` documents as the *single* home for this wording. As a result the packet header re-states the mismatch in its own `format!` and re-reads `manifest.rules_v`/`crate::canon::RULES_V` instead of the values the guard actually compared. The concrete risk: `RulesMismatch::reason()` is explicitly documented as one function "rather than a `format!` per call site" because the wording (and the remedy direction) must not drift; a later reword of the reason leaves this header — and the Findings line in the same packet — describing the same state two different ways. Storing `Option<baseline::RulesMismatch>` (it is `Copy`) in `Coverage` lets both places render from one source.
findings.title: maintainability

findings.text: When a signature/trust failure also exists, the mismatch reas……on is dropped entirely, so `baseline --verify` reports only the failure while `audit --baseline` reports both — the two surfaces disagree about what they tell a reader. Keep the reason by appending it to `failed` in that branch; the exit class is still FAIL, but the open question is no longer hidden.
findings.title: Keep mismatch reason beside other failures
